uncited: XPR-LinPrim Culling is a primitive-level early discard method for point-based volume rendering that uses a global bound on the maximum ray chord length through a primitive to determine if it can be discarded for an entire tile.
It eliminates the need for a separate per-pixel opacity test by leveraging the homogeneous density model of linear splats, where opacity is determined by the integral of density along the ray chord.
Unlike [Stop-the-pop](1472-stop-the-pop.md), which bounds the Gaussian response based on distance to the mean, LinPrim bounds the longest possible chord through the primitive's $L_1$ polytope.

- **Input**: Primitive density $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$, tile geometry $\Omega_t$ (defined by pixel center bounds $[x_{min}, x_{max}) \times [y_{min}, y_{max})$), and alpha threshold $\alpha_{\text{thresh}}$.
The method relies on the geometric definition of the primitive's support.
For linear splats, the primitive is defined by an $L_1$ polytope.
The geometry is characterized by four slab pairs, indexed by $i \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$.
where $\varepsilon_{i,0} = +1$ is fixed, and $\varepsilon_{i,1}, \varepsilon_{i,2} \in \{+1, -1\}$.
The vectors $\boldsymbol{c}_0, \boldsymbol{c}_1, \boldsymbol{c}_2$ define the orientation and scale of the primitive in screen space.
**Compute Half-Chord Lengths**: For each slab pair $i \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, calculate the minimum half-chord length $h_i$ over the tile $\Omega_t$.
This value represents the maximum distance from the slab center to the boundary along the ray direction, constrained by the tile bounds.
If the slab normal's z-component $n_{i,z} \neq 0$, the bounds are derived from solving $|\boldsymbol{n}_i \cdot (\Delta x, \Delta y, \tau)| \le 1$ for the depth parameter $\tau$.
**Calculate Primitive-Level Bound**: Compute the global primitive-level bound on the chord length.
This is derived from the case where $i=j$ in the general tile-bound equation, reducing to $g_{ii} = 2h_i$.
**Compare and Cull**: Compare the opacity bound against the threshold derived from the alpha threshold.
If this inequality holds, the primitive is discarded for all pixels in the tile.
- **Loose Bounds**: The bound can become loose when the constraint attaining the maximum chord length changes across the tile $\Omega_t$.
Bounds the Gaussian response based on distance to the mean.
Choose when using Gaussian splats. [1472-stop-the-pop](1472-stop-the-pop.md)
- **Time Complexity**: O(1) per primitive per tile, as it involves a constant number of slab pair checks (4) and a single comparison.
- **Memory Complexity**: O(1) auxiliary memory.
XPR-LinPrim Culling was introduced in the XPR renderer paper.
It is based on the linear-splatting culling method used in the reference CUDA linear-splatting implementation.
